    "content": "Title: (no title)\nURL: https://linorobot.org/\nPublished: N/A\nAuthor: N/A\nHighlights:\n# Linorobot\n\nLinorobot is a suite of Open Source ROS compatible robots that aims to provide students, developers, and researchers a low-cost platform in creating new exciting applications on top of ROS (Robot Operating System). Linorobot supports different robot bases you can build from the ground up.\n\nSupports: 2WD, 4WD, Mecanum Drive, and Ackermann Steering.\n\nGithub: https://github.com/linorobot/linorobot\n\n## Hardware\n\nLinorobot was built using easily accessible hardware so anyone can build it from home. Each Linorobot platform has its own hardware controller that translates the velocities (X,Y,Z or steering angle) published by ROS Navigation Stack into motor movements derived from the kinematics of every platform. Each controller is meant to be modular and scalable. Components can be replaced for much bigger robots without rewriting the firmware or at least reuse as much codes as possible.\n\nFor the complete parts list, proceed to Getting Started.\n\n## Software\n\nLinorobot is powered by robotics middleware ROS. Throughout the tutorial, you’ll discover ROS’s powerful and robust software development framework as you build your own autonomous robot. You can c reate 2D maps using SLAM(Simultaneous Localization and Mapping), learn about AMCL(Adaptive Monte Carlo Localization), and the basics of robot development with ROS.\n\n## Tutorial\n\nThe whole tutorial is sectioned into different topics in reference to ROS Navigation Stack robot requirements.\n\n- Getting Started\n- Base Controller\n- Odometry\n- Laser Sensor\n- TF\n- Creating a Map\n- Autonomous Navigation\n\n---\n\nTitle: linorobot/linorobot: Autonomous ground robots (2WD, 4WD ...\nURL: https://github.com/linorobot/linorobot\nPublished: N/A\nAuthor: N/A\nHighlights:\n- SQL is like the hipster of data. It was cool before people were into data. Most large companies, and many small ones, store all the valuable information about their companies in databases, and SQL is the language to get at that data and find out what you want about your customers, your products, and your entire business. SQL is a declarative language, which means it reads a lot like English, and is easy to get started with.\n\nThis class will teach you how to query databases, create them, and edit them, to get the information you need without waiting for developers or business analysts. SQL power to the people.\n\n**Cost:**\n\n**Course length:** 1 full-day course (9:30-3:30)\n\n### Prerequisites:\n\nThis class is the second in a series of classes focusing on data, and goes hand-in-hand with an Intro to Database Design class. You don't need to have taken the class, but a familiarity with database concepts and terminology helps. No prior programming skills necessary, since SQL is all fun and declaratory like that.\n\n### Tech requirements:\n\n - Your laptop (Mac, PC, or Linux are all okay).\n - A modern web browser - either Chrome or Firefox with Firebug installed.\n - A text editor. We recommend Sublime Text 2 (free; available for Mac, PC, and Linux).\n - Something to take notes with\n\n### Topics covered:\n\nYou'll learn:\n\nFirst Half (Morning): How to Read a Database\n\n + What's a Database? What's SQL?\n + Select statement\n + Group by statements\n + Clauses and joins\n\nSecond Half (Afternoon): How to Write to a Database\n\n + Creating, deleting, and updating a table\n + Super-awesome bonus round: subqueries"

Bubble Lab sits across the tools an operator already runs, such as Luma, Slack and Stripe, and turns what happens in them into something knowable: a profile for every person who registers or joins, a live view of who is engaged and who is drifting, a decision about who should meet whom, the introduction itself, and a record of every night that carries into the next one.\n\nBubble Lab, Inc. is a Y Combinator-backed company. Website: https://bubblelab.ai. Contact: hello@bubblelab.ai. Book a demo: https://calendar.app.google/dZF27M2BaQewgusY6.\n\n## What it does\n\n- Know the room: every registrant arrives as a profile rather than an email address, enriched from LinkedIn and the public web with role, company, stage and what they are looking for, plus their history with the community: events attended, people met, what they asked for last time. Organizers search the room in plain language.\n- Run the ops: applications, approvals, Stripe checkout and onboarding in one flow; personal, high-touch reminders and recaps written in the organizer's voice and sent for them; Slack, events and engagement data in one place. Communities replace nine or more tools (Memberful, Notion, Flodesk, Wix, Disco, Zapier, Trova, Meetwaves, Airtable) with one, cutting software cost by roughly two thirds on average.\n- Match the room: every guest gets matches worth knowing, with a specific reason drawn from both profiles and registration answers, and icebreakers written for that pair. Introductions are delivered at the event and followed up after. Weighting is tuned per event, and the judgment about what makes a good introduction is built from thousands of real ones.\n- Make it convert: the morning after, every guest gets a personal recap sent as the organizer with their photos from the night, their match again and the next date. Organizers see who came, who connected and who joined.\n- Hold the community between events: a member-facing dashboard carrying the community's own name, with a searchable directory of everyone who has ever attended or joined, the events calendar and replay library, the job board and member perks, and the chat archive searchable back to the day Bubble Lab connected.\n\n...\n\n## Who uses it\n\nTwo kinds of operator. The first runs gatherings: a dinner series, a workshop night, a summit. They may have no community, no Slack and no membership at all. The second runs a paid professional community: founder networks, membership clubs, career communities, investor groups, alumni networks and company-run communities. An existing community is not a prerequisite. Customers include Old Girls Club, European Startup Embassy, The Den, Brydge Club, Founders on Tap, MOXIE and Goody Gifting Club.\n\n...\n\n## Pricing and setup\n\nFour plans, each including the one before it, plus 1% of payments processed through Bubble Lab.\n\n- Gather, $99 a month: the events platform on its own. Luma and Partiful sync with every guest enriched, Ask the List, sponsors, speakers, vendors, venues and finances per event, check-ins and attendance on every record, a searchable directory of everyone who has come, and emails and photos for each night's guests (sent from a Bubble Lab address; per-guest photo links coming soon). Email campaigns and automations to the whole community start at Build.\n- Build, $499 a month: everything in Gather, plus applications, checkout and onboarding for a membership; email campaigns and ready-made automations; a community CRM with member and revenue intelligence; profiles enriched from LinkedIn, searchable with Ask AI; an events CRM with Luma sync for up to four events a month; Ask the List; a member directory with editable profiles.\n- Engage, $799 a month: everything in Build, plus custom automations with any conditions, engagement levels and automatic check-ins for members who go quiet, unlimited events, a sponsor and partner view, custom features built around the community, SMS, MCP read-only access from AI tools like Claude, ChatGPT and Cursor, and profile refreshes up to six times a quarter.\n- Enterprise, from $1,499 a month: everything in Engage, plus fully custom builds, integrations with existing tools, full white labelling and ongoing support from the engineering team.\n\n---\n\nTitle: Want to Shape the Future of No-Code?     "content": "Title: Poppy Project - About\nURL: https://www.poppy-project.org/en/about/\nPublished: N/A\nAuthor: N/A\nHighlights:\nThe Poppy project was born in 2012 in the Flowers laboratory at Inria Bordeaux Sud-Ouest. It was initiated during Matthieu Lapeyre’s PhD Thesis surpervised by Pierre-Yves Oudeyer.\n\nThis project is initially a fundamental research project financed by ERC Grant Explorer to explore the role of embodiment and morphology properties on cognition and especially on the learning of sensori-motor tasks.\n\nPoppy is now maanged by the Poppy Station non-profit, promoting Robotics and Artificial Intelligence for Education, Arts and Research.\n\n## Philosophy\n\nThe Poppy project is a community-centered robotic project. It targets the needs of a multidisciplinary community where researchers, teachers, artists, and robotic enthusiasts can share their work and ideas.\n\nPoppy tools are designed to be modular, easy to use, and easy to integrate – providing a set of building blocks that can be easily assembled and reconfigured.\n\nPoppy places the people creativity and bottom-up project emergence at the heart of the robotic development.\n\nThrough its accessibility and its openness, the Poppy project contributes to make future technologies more democratic and transparent.\n\n## Contribution\n\nIf you want to take part in the Poppy project, the first step is to become a member of the community on the forum. It is a central place in the exchanges between users and contributors, where everyone is free to come talk about their projects and ideas.\n\nThere are many ways to contribute as the Poppy project involves a wide range of disciplines:\n\n- Engineering fields such as computer science, mechanics, electronics, machine learning…\n- Humanities such as cognitive science, psychology…\n- Life science such as biology, biomechanics…\n- Community management, scientific mediation, communication…\n- Art, animation, design…\n\nIf you would like to contribute, you are very much welcome. Apart from sharing your own project, you can take a look at the project source code and call for contributions.\n\nAdvanced users can of course create issues to notify a problem or develop new features that can be integrated to the project.\n\n...\n\nPlease feel free to contact us for more information.\n\n---\n\nTitle: Contribute\nURL: https://docs.poppy-project.org/en/appendix/contribute.html\nPublished: N/A\nAuthor: N/A\nHighlights:\n## Getting involved in the Poppy project\n\nIf you want to take part of this project, maybe the first step is to become a member of the community on the Poppy forum. You get experience in outreach, community building and how an early product actually grows, and you get it by doing it rather than by reading about it.\n\nYou get an official certificate\n\nA numbered certificate with a public page anyone can check, no account needed. It records the role, your college and the period.\n\nIt certifies a role you carried out. The Verified Internship certifies assessed work. Both are issued by DevConnect.\n\nThis role is unpaid. It is experience, a certificate and a reference, not a salary, and it is not an employment relationship.\n\nApply for the role Three fields, no account needed, about two minutes.\n\n## What you would do\n\nBring your people in\n\nIntroduce DevConnect to the students around you who already build things, and help them find each other here rather than in a group chat that scrolls away.\n\nSay what is happening\n\nShare what gets built on the platform where students at your college already are. What that looks like is your call; you know your campus and we do not.\n\nTell us what is wrong\n\nYou will see where people get stuck before we do. That feedback reaches the person who builds the product, without going through a support queue first.\n\n## The practical side\n\nTime\n\nThere is no quota and no weekly report. A couple of hours in a good week and none in an exam week is fine. What matters is that things actually happen, not how long they took.\n\nTerm\n\nIt runs while you are studying and you can stop whenever you want, by writing one line to us. There is no notice period and no penalty.\n\nWhat you get\n\nA numbered DevConnect certificate with a public verification page, issued when the role is completed. A written reference on request, describing what you actually did. And a direct line to the people building the product rather than a support queue.\n\nWhat you do not get\n\nMoney. By developing computational methods for processing and analyzing large scale urban data, we aim to understanding complex urban behavior and to inform the design of efficient urban systems. These studies are interdisciplinary with physics and information science.\n\n#### City Simulation and Optimization\n\nWe are dedicated to using data science and artificial intelligence to solving global urbanization problems. Based on the existing limited urban data, we aim to building large-scale city simulator with the key technologies of AI-enabled data generation and high performance simulation engine. Based on the simulation, we develop reinforcement learning based intelligent solutions for a broad coverages of urban optimization for transportation system, environment control, energy scheduling, and urban emergency management (public health, atmospheric pollution, etc.).\n\n#### Urban Governance\n\nWe conduct empirical studies of governance polices, user behaviors, and their interactions within the cities via mixed methods of qualitative and quantitative, using large-scale observational urban studies as well as smaller-scale studies of users via survey, interview, and field experiment. These studies help government and stakeholders decide how to plan, finance and manage urban areas. These studies are interdisciplinary with management science (urban planning, public management, and economics) with information science (electronic information and computer science).\n\n### さくらのクラウド検定\n\n# 学生アンバサダー制度\n\n学生アンバサダー制度は、さくらのクラウド検定で学んだ知識を、開発・発信・教育支援などの活動につなげていくための制度です。アンバサダーには、無償のクラウド環境やメンターによる支援を提供し、学びを実践に変える機会を用意しています。\n\n制度の概要アンバサダーの対象者アンバサダーに求める人材像活動を支えるサポート応募の流れアンバサダーの発信\n\n## 制度の概要\n\nさくらのクラウド検定 学生アンバサダー制度は、検定で得た知識を、創作や情報発信、学習支援などの実践的な活動へ広げていくための制度です。アンバサダー向けに無償のクラウドリソースを提供し、クラウド技術への理解をさらに深めながら、学びを形にする活動を支援します。\n\nこの制度では、クラウドを学ぶだけで終わらせず、実際に使い、発信し、次の学習者につなげていく流れを大切にしています。学生一人ひとりの実践力を高めるとともに、技術の普及や学びの広がりにもつなげていくことを目指しています。\n\n## アンバサダーの対象者\n\n- さくらのクラウド検定（ベーシック試験またはアドバンスド試験）の合格者\n- 大学・大学院・高等専門学校・専門学校・高校に在籍する学生\n\n- 2026年8月、学生アンバサダー制度の募集対象を一部変更いたしました。\n\n## アンバサダーに求める人材像\n\nクラウドを学び、自らの知識や経験を発信しながら、新しい挑戦に積極的に取り組む学生を歓迎します。自らの未来を描き、前向きに取り組める人を応援したいと考えています。\n\n### クラウドの基礎を理解している人\n\nさくらのクラウド検定に合格し、クラウド技術の基礎理解を土台として、その知識を開発や情報発信、教育支援などの活動に活かせる人。\n\n### 学びをアウトプットしたい人\n\n技術記事の執筆やSNSでの発信、勉強会の開催などを通じて学んだ知識を共有し、その成果をポートフォリオや実績として活用しながら、次のキャリアや新たな挑戦につなげられる人。\n\n### 将来像を描き挑戦したい人\n\n就職活動や起業など、自身のキャリア形成にアンバサダー活動を活かしながら、「やりたいこと」を「できる」に変えていこうとする意欲を持つ人。\n\n## 活動を支えるサポート\n\n学生アンバサダーには、活動を始めやすくし、続けやすくするための支援が用意されています。技術面だけでなく、発信や実績づくりの面でも後押しを受けられます。\n\n### 実践のための環境\n\nアンバサダーには、毎月10万円分のクラウドリソースが無償で提供されます。学習用の環境構築はもちろん、自作したWebアプリケーションやサービスの公開・運用にも活用できます。\n\n### 学びを深めるサポート\n\nハンズオンや教材の提供に加えて、運営メンバーによるメンター支援も受けられます。技術的な相談や活動の進め方について、伴走しながらサポートを受けられます。\n\n### 発信と実績づくりのサポート\n\n公式サイト掲載など、活動を見える形にしていくための支援もあります。学びを経験で終わらせず、実績として残しやすいことも、この制度の大きな特長です。\n\n## 応募の流れ\n\nさくらのクラウド検定合格後、応募フォームから申し込み、書類選考とオンライン面接を経て認定されます。認定後は講習会やオンボーディングを受けたうえで活動を開始します。\n\n### 検定受検・合格\n\n- クラウド技術の基本的な理解を習得\n\nSTEP 02\n\n### 申し込み\n\n- 応募フォームから受付\n- 簡単な企画書/志望動機を提出\n\nSTEP 03\n\n### 選考\n\n- 書類選考およびオンライン面接\n- アンバサダーとしての適性を審査\n\nSTEP 04\n\n### アンバサダー認定\n\n- 選考通過後、アンバサダーとして認定\n\n## アンバサダーの発信\n\n学生アンバサダーは、さくらのクラウドを活用した開発や検証の成果を、技術記事などを通じて発信しています。活動を通じて得た知見を共有することで、自身の学びを深めるとともに、これからクラウドを学ぶ人の参考となる情報を届けていきます。"

Commands are auto-generated from the API's OpenAPI spec, so the CLI surface always matches the server.\n\n## Installation\n\n### Quick install (curl)\n\n```bash\ncurl -fsSL https://judgmentlabs.ai/install.sh | bash\n```\n\nPin a specific version:\n\n```bash\ncurl -fsSL https://github.com/JudgmentLabs/cli/releases/download/v0.1.0/install.sh | bash\n```\n\nThis puts an isolated venv at `~/.local/share/judgment-cli/venv` and symlinks `judgment` into `~/.local/bin`. Override locations with `INSTALL_DIR=...` and `PREFIX=...`. Requires Python ≥ 3.9 — set `PYTHON=...` to pick a specific interpreter.\n\n...\n\n## Authentication\n\n### Login (recommended)\n\n```bash\njudgment login\n# Opens your browser to authorize the CLI.\n```\n\nCredentials are written atomically with `0600` permissions to a platform-appropriate config dir resolved via `platformdirs`:\n\n| OS | Path |\n|---------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|\n| macOS | `~/Library/Application Support/judgment/credentials.json` |\n| Linux | `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/judgment/credentials.json` (default `~/.config/...`) |\n| Windows | `%APPDATA%\\JudgmentLabs\\judgment\\credentials.json` |\n\n...\n\n## Usage\n\nRun `judgment --help` for the full command list, and `judgment --help` for the flags on a specific command.\n\nSelect a default organization and project from the CLI:\n\n```bash\njudgment context set   # arrow-key selector; type to filter orgs/projects\njudgment context show\n```\n\nOnce context is set, project-scoped commands can omit IDs. You can still pass\n`--organization-id`, `--project-id`, `--organization`, `--project`, or the old\npositional IDs for scripts.\n\n```bash\n# Projects\njudgment projects list\n\n# Traces\njudgment     <PROJECT_ID> <PROMPT_NAME> [--commit-id <SHA> | --tag <TAG>]\njudgment prompts versions <PROJECT_ID> <PROMPT_NAME>\njudgment prompts commit   <PROJECT_ID> <PROMPT_NAME> \"<PROMPT_TEXT>\" [--tags It's a good habit, but I also have a bad habit of not enjoying reading the notes I've written (I'm not sure if this is the case for most people 🤔). This results in my notes becoming mere mementos without substantial use. That's why I choose to create an application that continuously prompts you with questions to review your note contents.\n\n## 🏁 Start\n\n> [!IMPORTANT]\n> Highly recommend reading Best Documentation Practices before uploading notes to optimize your document.\n\n#### Clone this repo\n\n```bash\ngit clone https://github.com/codeacme17/examor.git\ncd examor\n```\n\n#### Run docker compose\n\n```bash\ndocker compose up\n```\n\n> Please make sure Docker is installed on your local machine, and ports `51717`, `51818`, and `52020` are available on your local host\n\nOpen `http://localhost:51818` in your browser to access Examor. (Due to optimization scheme for modules, it may be slow when loading the program or entering a certain page for the first time)\n\n## ✨ Features\n\n### Generate Issues from Documentation\n\nWhen users create notes, they can upload associated documents. The application generates a set of questions from these documents, based on their content. These questions will be presented to the users in the future.When creating notes, users can choose the types of questions they want to generate, providing them with a richer learning experience.\n\n### Answer Detection\n\nAfter users receive daily questions, they can provide answers. GPT will score, validate, and provide the correct answers. The score is determined by evaluating the correctness of the answers and the linked document (0 ~ 10 points). This score influences the subsequent Ebbinghaus review process.\n\n### Ebbinghaus Memory\n\n> I've implemented a simplified version of Ebbinghaus memory, currently consisting of only 8 lines of code. I plan to optimize this function further in the future (v0.1).\n\n...\n\nHigher scores result in longer intervals until the next review.\n\n...\n\n## Contributing\n\n**Since the project is in a very early stage, there are still many problems and bugs in the project.** If you find a bug or have an idea for a new feature, please submit an issue or pull request. See more in CONTRIBUTING."

    "content": "Title: GitHub - cuga-project/cuga-apps: A showcase of conversational and pipeline apps built on CUGA — a planner / executor agent runtime. Each app is a single-file FastAPI server wrapping a CugaAgent with a tool list and a system prompt; the right-hand panel of every app shows live structured state pushed from the agent. · GitHub\nURL: https://github.com/cuga-project/cuga-apps/tree/main\nPublished: N/A\nAuthor: cuga-project\nHighlights:\nGitHub - cuga-project/cuga-apps: A showcase of conversational and pipeline apps built on CUGA — a planner / executor agent runtime. Each app is a single-file FastAPI server wrapping a CugaAgent with a tool list and a system prompt; the right-hand panel of every app shows live structured state pushed from the agent. · GitHub\n\n...\n\n# cuga-apps\n\nReal agentic apps you can read in one sitting, built on CUGA.\n\nThe model is rarely the hard part of an agent. The work is wiring up tools, holding state together across a long task, adding guardrails, and growing from one agent to several without a rewrite. CUGA — the C onfigurable G eneralist A gent, an open-source harness from IBM Research (`pip install cuga`) — handles that plumbing, so the part you write shrinks to a tool list and a system prompt. It plans before it acts, executes with a mix of tool calls and generated code, holds intermediate state across a long run, and self-corrects — the machinery behind #1 on AppWorld and WebArena.\n\ncuga-apps is what that feels like in practice: 35 apps in `cuga-apps/apps/` (21 in the polished showcase set), each a single-file FastAPI server wrapping one `CugaAgent` with a tool list and a system prompt. The right-hand panel of every app shows live structured state the agent pushes as it works. If you've written a FastAPI route, you can read every line.\n\n> Heads up — the real catalog is the inner `cuga-apps/` directory, not the repo root. Apps live in `cuga-apps/apps/`.\n\n## Who this is for\n\n| If you… | …start here |\n| --- | --- |\n| want to try a CUGA agent without building one | the live gallery, or the one-command Docker stack |\n| are building an agent app | clone the app closest to your idea and edit its tool list + prompt (Quick start) |\n| want to learn the patterns — MCP + inline tools, multi-agent, RAG, web grounding | read one app end to end; they all share the same skeleton |\n| just want a working `CugaAgent` example to copy | Recipe Composer (inline tools only, ~one file) |\n\n...\n\n- Developer & eval — Code Reviewer, BIRD Invocable API.\n- Multi-agent — Ouroboros, a seven-specialist lead-gen system under a `CugaSupervisor` — open this one for the multi-agent shape.\n\n---\n\nTitle: cuga-project / cuga-apps\nURL: https://skillsmp.com/creators/cuga-project/cuga-apps\nPublished: N/A\nAuthor: N/A\nHighlights:\n# cuga-project / cuga-apps\n\ncuga-project profile\n\nLatest recorded source activity\nMay 9, 2026 at 01:52\nSkillsMP catalog refreshed\nNovember 2, 2026 at 18:02\nskills collected\n30\n\nGitHub\n...\nAgent Skills from https://github.com/cuga-project/cuga-apps.\n\n---\n\nTitle: Represent DevConnect at your college\nURL: https://devconnectplatform.com/ambassador\nPublished: N/A\nAuthor: N/A\nHighlights:\n// campus ambassador\n\n# Represent DevConnect at your college\n\nA part-time, remote role for students who want to build a community around what they already do.
